clue.text: Not cheap to move memorial

indicators.note: the letters of 'not cheap' are told to move, so they shift into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters of the phrase are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone baulks at the cost of relocating a monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not cheap' reads as a comment on the price, but it is simply the eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a monument honouring war dead whose bodies lie elsewhere, a kind of memorial.

clue.text: Top talent's potential

parts.note: a cap is a lid or top
talent is natural ability

explanation.surface: A talent scout praises the promise of a leading performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective praising the talent, but it is the noun, a lid; the 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Capability and potential both mean latent power or capacity to achieve something; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Lace fruit carrier's no joke

indicators.note: saying the carrier has no joke means the word for a joke is taken out of it

parts.note: a punnet is a small basket for soft fruit such as strawberries
a pun is a joke on words; it is the part removed

explanation.surface: A shopper insists that a trimmed fruit basket is a serious matter.
explanation.walkthrough: A punnet is the small box British shops sell strawberries in; strip PUN from its front and NET is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Net is a mesh fabric, and lace is an openwork fabric of the same family, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Bridge designer to allow elevated crossing point

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: to let is to allow
a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

explanation.surface: An engineer is asked to permit a raised crossing, fittingly for a bridge builder.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Telford was a Scottish civil engineer who built the Menai Suspension Bridge; 'to' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Telford was a celebrated nineteenth century engineer famous for roads, canals and bridges, so he is one example.

clue.text: Areas for grazing antelopes supporting historical Sumerian city

indicators.note: in a down clue, something supporting sits underneath, so the antelopes come after the city

parts.note: historical things belong to the past
Ur was an ancient city of Sumer
elands are large African antelopes

explanation.surface: Grazing antelopes hold up the ruins of an ancient Mesopotamian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur is the crossword's favourite ancient city; 'historical' has to be turned into a noun, PAST, to sit on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasturelands are fields of grass where livestock feed, exactly places set aside for grazing animals.

clue.text: Plenty returned before space taken

indicators.note: one piece placed before another sets the order in which they are joined
something returned goes back the way it came, so the word runs right to left

parts.note: lots means plenty
an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A lot of goods came back before anyone noticed the room had been emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: En (and em) are printers' spaces, a common crossword source for EN and EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen and taken share the sense of removed without permission, the past participle of theft.

clue.text: Social media platform spreading hatred with society

indicators.note: letters that are spreading are scattered out of their original order

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A complaint that an online network spreads hatred through society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with society' simply adds S to the rearranged letters; the surface reads as a familiar complaint about social media.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads is the text-based social network launched by Meta in 2023, one example of such a platform.

clue.text: Eccles fine, I fancy, in biochemistry?

indicators.note: 'fancy' as a verb of imagining invites the letters to be reimagined in a new order

parts.note: the setter's name plus 'fine' and 'I', eleven letters

explanation.surface: The setter, Eccles, reckons he would do well in a biochemistry lab.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is the setter's pseudonym, so the name in the clue is fodder; the question mark marks biochemistry as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Biochemistry studies the chemistry of living organisms, so it is one branch of the life sciences.

clue.text: Distinction in nanotechnology

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following long word, spelled out in sequence

parts.note: found in letters three to six of the long word

explanation.walkthrough: Four consecutive letters of nanotechnology, starting after 'na', spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Note means eminence or renown, as in 'a writer of note', which is a sense of distinction.

clue.text: Brutal sex stops haemorrhoids scarring, initially

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so sex goes inside the haemorrhoids

parts.note: piles is the everyday word for haemorrhoids
'it' is a coy word for sex

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of scarring

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid tale of rough sex and a painful medical complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Piles is the everyday British word for haemorrhoids; 'it' as a coy word for sex is an old crossword favourite, from Kipling's era.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiless means showing no mercy or compassion, which is what brutal means; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Return for match

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for
to fit is to match, as clothes match a body

explanation.surface: A tennis player's shot back in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return for match' sounds like tennis or a rematch; 'for' looks like a link word but it is PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A return on an investment is the gain it produces, so return and profit are synonyms in finance.

clue.text: When communist is beginning to talk about 'Our Katie Perry', perhaps

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here of 'talk'

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
Trot is short for Trotskyist
taken as printed
taken as printed
the opening letter of talk
surface padding: it loosely lets the next two pieces come round after 'Our'

explanation.surface: A left-wing pundit starts discussing a pop star as if she were a national treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' has IST come round to follow OUR. Katy Perry, spelt Katie here, flew on a short Blue Origin space flight in 2025.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity paying for a brief trip into space is a space tourist, and Perry is one example.

clue.text: Serbians upset with lousy fellow European citizens

indicators.note: upset things are knocked over and end up in disorder

parts.note: eight letters of fodder
five more letters joined on by 'with'

explanation.surface: Serbians are annoyed at being lumped with some unpleasant neighbours from elsewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lousy' tempts as the indicator, but it is fodder; 'upset' does the work on both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Byelorussians, now usually Belarusians, are the people of Belarus, fellow citizens of Europe like the Serbians.

clue.text: Tear up terms for fixing old hearing aids

indicators.note: fixing something rebuilds it, so the letters are put together afresh

parts.note: eleven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: An instruction to scrap the contract for repairing antique hearing devices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear up' looks like the anagram signal, but those letters are fodder along with 'terms'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear trumpet is a horn-shaped device once held to the ear by the hard of hearing, before electronic aids.

clue.text: One leaving concerning opinion results in bad feeling

indicators.note: the letter for one departs from the word for opinion

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
one is the Roman numeral I, the letter that goes
sentiment is an opinion; take out the I

explanation.surface: Someone who quits over a disagreement leaves hard feelings behind.
explanation.walkthrough: SENTIMENT loses its second I; RE goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is bitterness felt at unfair treatment, a synonym for bad feeling between people.

clue.text: Periodically loud, clear and bright

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of 'loud' is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of loud
to clear a place is to rid it of something

explanation.surface: A description of a sound or colour that is now and then loud, sharp and vivid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' seems to govern the whole phrase, but it works only on 'loud'; 'clear' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid describes glaring, garish colours, so a lurid shade is vividly bright, a synonym.

clue.text: Noise made in speech from Earl, belligerent after losing silver

definitions.note: egressive is chiefly an adjective; as a noun it names such a sound

indicators.note: the belligerent word loses a chunk, the symbol for silver

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Earl
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, the part removed
aggressive means belligerent; drop the AG

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome aristocrat makes a noise after pawning the family silver.
explanation.walkthrough: AGGRESSIVE loses its opening AG, and E for Earl goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an egressive is a sound produced by pushing air outward from the lungs, as most spoken sounds are.

clue.text: Scold Republican supporter of Trump entering shelter

indicators.note: things entering a shelter go inside it

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a MAGA supporter backs Trump's Make America Great Again movement

explanation.surface: A Republican partisan gets told off as he ducks into cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scold' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a nagging person. MAGA stands for Trump's slogan Make America Great Again.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, overbearing woman, and a scold in the old sense is a nagging, quarrelsome woman.

clue.text: Mostly free

definitions.meaning: the phrase meaning generally or as a whole, as said of the public
the phrase used of an escaped prisoner still roaming uncaught

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two senses of the same phrase; 'Mostly' tempts as a deletion signal, but nothing follows for it to act on.
explanation.definitionFit: 'At large' means in general, broadly, and also means roaming uncaptured, as a fugitive does.

clue.text: John Doe's day out in boat

indicators.note: the day is put out, removed from the name that follows John

parts.note: john and can are both American slang for a toilet
D abbreviates day
Doe without its D

explanation.surface: An anonymous everyman spends a day off out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John Doe' reads as one name, the American placeholder for an unknown man, but the two words split: John is a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light, narrow boat paddled by hand, so it is a type of boat.

clue.text: Food provider of, say, Queen Elizabeth II, the former monarch

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so a queen is one example of a cat
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was her royal cipher
'the former' points back to the monarch just named, so ER again

explanation.surface: A question about who fed the late Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Elizabeth II' reads as one royal, but Queen splits off as a cat. 'The former' is the old usage for the first of things mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer is a business or person supplying meals for events, which is exactly a food provider.

clue.text: Mother and son only intended to suppress a problem dealing with society

indicators.note: to suppress something is to keep it from appearing, so the a vanishes

parts.note: ma is mother
a lad is a boy or son
just means only
meant means intended; drop the A
the letter removed

explanation.surface: A mother and son cover up a social problem they would rather not discuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother and son' suggests M and S, but son here is LAD. MEANT loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladjustment is a failure to cope with the demands of one's social environment, a difficulty in handling society.

clue.text: Small milk container is lighter

parts.note: S abbreviates small, as on clothing labels
a cow holds milk, playfully seen as a container

explanation.surface: A little jug of milk weighs less than a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' looks like an adjective about weight, but it is a noun: a barge used to unload ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat for carrying cargo, and a lighter is the same kind of barge.

clue.text: Fruit in cold alcoholic drink with no head

indicators.note: a drink with no head has lost its top, its opening letter

parts.note: C marks cold on taps
sherry is a fortified wine; drop its first letter

explanation.surface: A cherry garnishing a chilled cocktail with no froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no head' sounds like a flat beer, but it removes the S from SHERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry is a small round stone fruit, so it is one example of fruit.

clue.text: Eccles's corn, reportedly, is debilitating malady

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: the setter speaking of his corn says 'my grain'

explanation.surface: The setter complains that a corn on his foot is crippling him.
explanation.walkthrough: Corn looks like the foot complaint, fitting the malady, but it is grain; Eccles is the setter, so his is 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe recurring headache, often with nausea, that can leave sufferers unable to work.

clue.text: I use derivative of Esperanto

parts.note: taken as printed
to do drugs is to use them

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to using a spin-off of Esperanto.
explanation.walkthrough: Ido is an invented language, a reformed version of Esperanto created in 1907.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido was built by reformers who modified Esperanto, so it is an offshoot of that constructed language.

clue.text: Flat ring used to be in this place, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: was is the past of to be
here means in this place; drop the final E

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that a flat ring used to sit here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat ring' could suggest a doorbell in an apartment; here it is a hardware disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A washer is a thin flat disc with a hole, placed under a nut or bolt head, a flat ring.

clue.text: Begin as best-performing solicitor

parts.note: the star is the best performer
a tout solicits custom or sells tickets

explanation.surface: A new lawyer resolves to begin their career at the top of the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Solicitor suggests a British lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To start out means to set off or begin a journey or career, a phrasal synonym of begin.
